verified_by: 3-state differential (Maven, JDK 17) on an authored self-contained project (scratchpad/jackson-mimic)
note: Authored mimic for Jackson's default-typing default-deny (PolymorphicTypeValidator). Used because every EXTERNAL Jackson PTV adaptation found in mining is either framework-coupled (Spring Security session serialization, e.g. madgeek-arc/resource-catalogue) or a data-driven allowlist-widening (e.g. omprakash201194/kin-keeper), not a clean standalone version-driven break. See jackson-caveat below.

jackson_caveat.not_a_silent_behavioural_break: Unlike xstream 1.4.18 (which flipped the DEFAULT to deny, so unchanged code silently starts throwing), Jackson's change is primarily a COMPILE break: enableDefaultTyping() was deprecated in 2.10 and REMOVED in 2.12, forcing migration to activateDefaultTyping(PolymorphicTypeValidator). The deny-behaviour (ForbiddenClass-style) only appears once you OPT IN to a restrictive PTV.
jackson_caveat.why_mimic_varies_posture_not_version: Because the deny is opt-in, a pure library-VERSION differential with identical code cannot demonstrate it (old code doesn't compile on the new version). The mimic therefore varies the security POSTURE the upgrade forces a developer to choose: permissive (LaissezFaire) -> restrictive PTV (default-deny) -> allowlisted PTV (adaptation). This is the faithful analogue of the xstream default-deny -> allowlist story.

external_evidence.bump_commits_are_visible: Unlike the transitive xstream/Axon cases, Jackson is a direct/BOM-managed dependency so version bumps ARE explicit commits, e.g. apache/spark 8eb8f747 (pom 2.9.10 -> 2.10.0, the PTV-introduction boundary), and many CVE-driven <jackson.version> edits.
real_ptv_adaptations: madgeek-arc/resource-catalogue@7f625e24 - SessionConfig.java introduces BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator, but routed through Spring Security session serialization (SecurityJacksonModules.getModules(loader, ptv)) and on Jackson 3 (tools.jackson) / Spring Boot 4 -> framework-coupled, not standalone-verifiable.

omprakash201194/kin-keeper@89eb519c - CacheConfig.java (native Maven) BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator allowlist, but the commit only WIDENS an existing allowlist (adds java.math) -> data-driven, not version-driven.

adaptation.summary: PaymentStore round-trips an Account (whose polymorphic holder is a Balance) through Jackson default typing. The adaptation is adaptedMapper(): a BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator that allowlists the app's own package, satisfying the default-deny validator.

behavioral_break.mechanism: Jackson default typing with a restrictive PolymorphicTypeValidator denies resolution of any class not on the allowlist during deserialization -> InvalidTypeIdException. Analogous to xstream 1.4.18 ForbiddenClassException.
behavioral_break.observed_exception: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.InvalidTypeIdException: Could not resolve type id 'mimic.Account' as a subtype of `mimic.Account`: Configured `PolymorphicTypeValidator` (of type `BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator`) denied resolution

verification.method: 3-state differential (Maven, JDK 17), Jackson 2.17.2 held constant, varying the production PaymentStore mapper factory (security posture).
verification.test: mimic.PaymentStoreBbcTest (JUnit5; round-trip Account, assert the Balance amount survives). Preserved in scratchpad/jackson-mimic/.

states.name: 2_new_lib_old_code
states.config: PaymentStore.securedUnadaptedMapper() (restrictive PTV, app package NOT allowlisted)
states.detail: InvalidTypeIdException: PolymorphicTypeValidator denied resolution of mimic.Account

verification.conclusion: Confirmed BBC (authored mimic): permissive default typing round-trips the app's own type; the default-deny posture rejects it with InvalidTypeIdException; the production allowlist (BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator over the app package) resolves it — the Jackson analogue of the xstream 1.4.18 default-deny -> allowlist adaptation.
